title: Broomstick lace scarf
excerpt: A classic long scarf worked in chunky yarn using broomstick lace. Groups of loops are stretched over a large dowel and worked off together to create the signature petal clusters.
sourceNotes: Broomstick lace stretches groups of crochet loops over a thick dowel or large knitting needle, then works them off in clusters to create a distinctive openwork pattern.

glossaryTerms.definition: A large loop formed by drawing up a stitch onto a thick dowel or jumbo knitting needle before working it off in a cluster.
The finished unit in broomstick lace: a group of enlarged loops (usually 4 or 5) slipped off the dowel and worked together with a double crochet into the base.

crochet.gaugeText: 2 clusters (10 sts) x 4 rows = 10 cm in broomstick lace on 6.0 mm hook with 25 mm dowel.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 20 cm wide x 160 cm long.

content.text: Broomstick lace works by drawing loops up onto a thick dowel to form
, then slipping them off in groups to make
. You need a 25 mm dowel or large knitting needle in addition to the crochet hook.
Chain 40. Row 1: 1 double crochet in 2nd chain from hook and in each chain to end (40 dc). Turn.

Row 2 (loop row): do not turn. Working right to left, insert hook in first st, pull up a large loop and place it on the dowel. Continue drawing up a loop from each stitch and placing on the dowel (40 loops on dowel). Row 3 (cluster row): slide 5 loops off the dowel onto the hook. Chain 1, work 5 double crochets through the centre of these 5 loops. Repeat across the row (8 clusters). Do not turn. Repeat rows 2 and 3 to length.
Work until the scarf reaches 160 cm. Fasten off and weave in the ends with the tapestry needle.
